summary: Read posthog.com/docs directly (getting-started/install, libraries/js/persistence, libraries/js/config, privacy/data-collection, product-analytics/capture-events, activity, api, api/queries, pricing) as of 2026-08-13. PostHog's current official static-HTML install is a single vanilla-JS loader snippet placed before </head>, loading array.js from a CDN derived from api_host. US Cloud values: api_host `https://us.i.posthog.com` (public/ingestion), ui_host/private-API host `https://us.posthog.com`. The officially recommended consent pattern is explicit: always load the snippet, initialize with `opt_out_capturing_by_default: true`, and call `posthog.opt_in_capturing()` / `posthog.opt_out_capturing()` from the CMP's consent-change callback — PostHog's docs explicitly warn against gating the script tag itself behind consent. An alternative fully-cookieless path (`cookieless_mode: "on_reject"`) needs no opt-in/opt-out wiring at all. Custom events use `posthog.capture('event_name', {props})`. Default persistence is `localStorage+cookie`, with the cookie named `ph_<project_api_key>_posthog` (365-day expiry); `persistence: 'memory'` or `disable_persistence: true` avoid storage entirely pre-consent. Verification is via the dashboard's Activity tab (Live view) or the private Query API (`POST {ui_host}/api/projects/:id/query/` with a personal API key, Bearer auth) or the raw public capture endpoint. Free tier on Product Analytics is 1,000,000 events/month free, with generous free tiers on 12 other products, no credit card required, 1 project / 1-year retention on the free plan.

findings.detail: Official 'JS snippet' install for plain HTML sites, shown on the Install PostHog doc page under the 'JS snippet' tab. Paste into <head> (or right before </body>) of every page. Replace <ph_project_token> with the real project API key (starts with phc_). The `defaults: '2026-05-30'` line pins current SDK default behaviors (a PostHog-specific versioned-defaults mechanism, not a real date value to change).

findings.topic: CDN script URL actually loaded by the snippet
findings.detail: The loader function derives the real asset URL from api_host at runtime: it replaces ".i.posthog.com" with "-assets.i.posthog.com" and appends "/static/array.js". For the US Cloud api_host `https://us.i.posthog.com`, this resolves to a concrete, fetchable CDN URL. This is dynamic (not a hardcoded <script src>) so it self-adjusts for EU Cloud or self-hosted api_host values too.
Used as the `api_host` value inside posthog.init(). Public POST-only endpoints (event capture, feature flags) live here and require no auth beyond the project token.

findings.topic: US Cloud ui_host / private API host
findings.detail: PostHog's docs state private GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE endpoints (querying, personal-API-key auth) live on a separate domain from the ingestion host. The `ui_host` init option exists specifically to point PostHog's own generated links (e.g. session replay/toolbar links) at the correct app URL, needed only when proxying api_host. For a direct (non-proxied) US Cloud install you generally don't need to set ui_host explicitly, but if you do, this is the value.
findings.code_or_values: https://us.posthog.com  (ui_host config key: string, default undefined, e.g. `ui_host: 'https://us.posthog.com'`)

findings.detail: Not requested as primary but confirmed on the same API overview page: EU Cloud public endpoint and private/app endpoint.

PostHog's docs explicitly warn: do NOT wrap/gate the <script> loader itself behind a consent-management-platform (CMP) rule, because then PostHog can't count visitors who dismiss the banner and can't react to a later consent change. Always load posthog-js unconditionally; control capturing via the SDK's own opt-in/opt-out API. Recommended flow: (1) init with opt_out_capturing_by_default: true so nothing is captured pre-consent; (2) on consent-accept, call posthog.opt_in_capturing(); (3) on consent-deny/withdraw, call posthog.opt_out_capturing(); wire both into whatever consent-change callback the CMP (OneTrust, Cookiebot, Osano, Usercentrics, or a custom banner) exposes.
Where the opt-out flag itself is stored (separate from event data) can be controlled independently.

findings.topic: Alternative: cookieless tracking mode (no opt-in/opt-out code needed)
findings.detail: Docs present this as an alternative to the opt_in/opt_out wiring: with cookieless_mode: 'on_reject', PostHog never stores cookies/localStorage until the user opts in, no events are captured pre-consent, and rejected/undecided users are still counted anonymously via a privacy-preserving server-side hash — all without you writing opt_in_capturing()/opt_out_capturing() calls. Requires enabling 'Cookieless server hash mode' in PostHog project settings (Project Settings > Web analytics) first. cookieless_mode: 'always' is the fully-cookieless variant with no banner needed at all (but you should avoid identify() calls in that mode).

Full list of `persistence` config values. 'memory' persists nothing beyond the page view — a common choice if you want the script loaded but non-persistent before consent, combined with dynamic switching via posthog.set_config() once the user answers the consent prompt.

findings.topic: Custom event capture for quote-form interactions
findings.detail: Standard capture() call. Docs recommend '[object] [verb]' naming (e.g. 'quote_form submitted'). Properties object is optional and freeform.

findings.topic: Cookies/localStorage keys PostHog sets (for cookie policy table)
findings.detail: PostHog stores: distinct_id, session ID & device ID, active/enabled feature flags, any registered 'super properties', and some SDK config flags (e.g. whether session recording is enabled). With the default persistence mode ('localStorage+cookie'), only the distinct_id and session ID go in an actual browser cookie; everything else goes to localStorage. The cookie name pattern and default lifetime are fixed.
findings.code_or_values:
Cookie name pattern: ph_<project_api_key>_posthog  |  Expiry: 365 days  |  Purpose: stores distinct_id + session ID (cross-subdomain identity)

localStorage keys use the same ph_<project_api_key>_posthog prefix and hold the bulk of the state (feature flags, super properties, config flags) under the 'localStorage+cookie' default persistence.

Optional: `cookie_persisted_properties: [...]` config lets you explicitly whitelist additional custom properties (e.g. signup_source) to also live in the cross-subdomain cookie via posthog.register().

findings.detail: If you don't want PostHog to write anything to the browser at all (e.g. before consent, or for anonymous-only tracking), disable_persistence is the hard switch — disables cookies, sessionStorage, and localStorage together. Caveat: you then must call posthog.identify() on every load or each refresh looks like a new user.

findings.topic: Verifying events arrive — dashboard Activity/Live view
findings.detail: PostHog's dashboard has an 'Activity' tab with multiple views, including a 'Live' view that shows a real-time feed of events as they're captured plus a count of currently active users; can be filtered to a single event name or paused. No API key needed for this, just log into the PostHog project UI. A companion terminal tool, `posthog-live`, streams live events to your CLI (installed via a GitHub release binary, then authenticates through the browser).
findings.code_or_values:
Dashboard path: Activity tab -> 'Live' view (filterable by event, pausable)

CLI install (macOS Apple Silicon):
curl -L https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/releases/download/posthog-live-latest/posthog-live-darwin-arm64 -o posthog-live && chmod +x posthog-live
./posthog-live --event-type "$pageview,$autocapture" --distinct-id "user_123"

findings.topic: Verifying events arrive — Query API with a personal API key
findings.detail: For programmatic verification, POST a HogQL query to the project's private query endpoint on the ui_host (app) domain, authenticated with a personal API key (created under user settings, needs 'Query Read' permission) as a Bearer token. Note this endpoint is rate-limited (2400/hour) and not intended as a bulk export mechanism — fine for a one-off 'did my event land' check.

findings.topic: Raw capture endpoint (alternate verification / non-JS ingestion)
findings.detail: The same public endpoint the SDK's array.js uses under the hood; useful to know for debugging network calls in devtools or sending events without JS. Uses the project token, not a personal API key, and needs no auth.

Two plans: Free (no card required, 1 project, 1-year data retention, community support) and pay-as-you-go Paid ($0/mo base, 6 projects, 7-year retention, email support) where every product carries its own free monthly tier that resets monthly and you pay only for overage. No per-seat charges either way. Product Analytics (what a quote-form/event-tracking build would use) free tier: first 1,000,000 events/month free.
findings.code_or_values:
Product analytics: first 1,000,000 events/mo FREE, then $0.00005/event (1,000,001-2,000,000), decreasing further at higher volume tiers down to $0.000009/event above 250M.
Session replay: first 5,000 recordings/mo free.
Feature flags & Experiments: first 1,000,000 requests/mo free.
Surveys: first 1,500 responses/mo free.
Error tracking: first 100,000 exceptions/mo free.
All prices USD, current as of this pricing page fetch (2026-08-13).

findings.topic: Autocapture (already-on by default, relevant to consent scope)
findings.detail: Out of the box (before any custom capture calls), the snippet also autocaptures pageviews, pageleaves, clicks, input changes, and form submissions on a/button/form/input/select/textarea/label elements. This is exactly what opt_out_capturing_by_default blocks until consent — relevant because a quote form's native <form> submission would otherwise be autocaptured pre-consent without the gating pattern above.
findings.code_or_values: posthog.init('<ph_project_token>', { api_host: 'https://us.i.posthog.com', autocapture: false }) // to fully disable if desired
